diagnostic_evidence.quote: All three methods exhibit a time complexity of $O(N^2)$ and outperform S-Fair-SC.
AFF-Fair-SMW incurred the highest overall runtime
our algorithms maintained an average balance comparable to S-Fair-SC

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims twice the speed and twice the balance of the state of the art, and the introduction claims all three variants run in O(N^2) and outperform S-Fair-SC. The Time Complexity section only gives a per-restart cost O(m+nh^2+h^3+nk^2) with no bound on restarts and no O(N^2) derivation. The experiments report balance as only 'comparable', no factor-two balance gain is shown, and several experiments (German, Facebook, Experiment 1 with small eigs share) show equal or worse runtime for some variants. 'Outperform' is therefore contradicted for AFF-Fair-SMW on German and for Sym/RW on several datasets.

failure_location.quote: We achieve an improvement in computation time that is twice as fast as the state-of-the-art, and also flexible enough to achieve twice as much balance.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claims to match the evidence: comparable balance, runtime gains for specific variants and sparse regimes, and a per-restart cost bound; remove or prove the O(N^2) and twice-as-balanced claims.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised quantitative guarantees (2x speed, 2x balance, O(N^2) complexity, uniform superiority over S-Fair-SC) are not established by the paper's content; only dataset-dependent speedups of one variant (AFF) are shown.
issues.title: Headline speed/balance/complexity claims (twice as fast, twice the balance, O(N^2), outperforms S-Fair-SC) are unsupported or contradicted by the paper's own experiments
issues.why_classification: No proof architecture changes, but the headline contributions must be materially weakened and the complexity claim either derived or dropped.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we suspect that the eigen-gap plays a critical role; preliminary analysis suggests a large eigen-gap in the sparse case, but further research is needed to confirm this.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction states as established that all three variants have a larger eigen gap than S-Fair-SC and that this reduces Arnoldi restarts. The paper contains no spectral-gap analysis of U versus the deflated S-Fair-SC operator, and later admits the role of the gap is only suspected. The Sym and RW variants are also reported with no consistent eigs speedup, contradicting 'all three'.

failure_location.quote: by introducing a larger eigen gap, which in turn reduces the number of restarts required in the Arnoldi restarting iterative method

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Present the eigen-gap explanation as a conjecture, or supply an actual gap comparison.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed explanation for the speedup is unsupported, so the abstract's 'different spectral gaps' narrative is conjecture.
issues.title: Eigen-gap/restart-reduction mechanism asserted as fact but never analysed
issues.why_classification: Rewording as a hypothesis preserves the empirical results and the method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: -1 & \text{ if } i\notin \bm{A}
Minimizing the cut function alone is known to isolate single nodes when performing graph partitions

issues.failure_explanation: For x in {+1,-1}^n, x^T D x = vol(V) is constant and x^T L x = 4 cut(A,B), so the quotient equals 4 cut/vol(V), which is just the (unnormalised) cut, not NCut = cut*vol(V)/(vol(A)vol(B)). The classical equivalence needs a two-valued vector with values depending on vol(A), vol(B) and the constraint x^T D 1 = 0. As written, the displayed equality min NCut = min Rayleigh quotient is false and contradicts the paper's own motivation for normalising.

failure_location.quote: It is well known \cite{shi2000normalized, pothen1990spectral} that this problem is equivalent to minimizing a specific form of the Rayleigh quotient:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the Shi-Malik indicator (values 1/vol(A) and -1/vol(B), or equivalent) and the constraint x^T D 1 = 0, or just cite the relaxation.
issues.overall_effect: The background derivation of the spectral relaxation is incorrect as stated, though the later k-way relaxation does not use it.
issues.title: NCut equals the Rayleigh quotient only for specially scaled indicators, not for the stated +/-1 vector
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the indicator definition fixes it; nothing downstream depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and using the fact that $Z^T=Z^{-1}$ we can reformulate this problem as follows:
where $Z$ is a projection to the null space of $F^T$ and $Z^TZ=I$
Notice that \eqref{SMW2} is equivalent to \eqref{SMW1} in the sense that the maximizer $H$ is the same.

issues.failure_explanation: Z is n x (n-h+1) with orthonormal columns, so it has no inverse and Z^T != Z^{-1}. The identity (Z^T G Z)^{-1} = Z^T G^{-1} Z is false in general: the compression of G^{-1} is the inverse of a Schur complement of G, not of the compression of G. Hence the eigenvectors of Z^T G Z for the largest eigenvalues need not be the eigenvectors of Z^T G^{-1} Z for the smallest, and the constrained maximisation of Tr(H^T G H) is not equivalent to the constrained minimisation of Tr(H^T G^{-1} H). Positivity of eigenvalues of Z^T G Z is also invoked for a general non-symmetric G.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the method must be re-derived and re-stated as solving min Tr(H^T G^{-1} H) s.t. F^T H=0 (a different objective), or a valid equivalence/approximation argument to (SMW1) must be supplied.
issues.overall_effect: The Fair-SMW objective (the U built from G^{-1}+mu FF^T) does not solve the stated problem (SMW1) for G; it solves a different problem (min Tr H^T G^{-1} H subject to F^T H=0). The method's motivation and its link to the original fair spectral relaxation are unsupported.
issues.title: Inversion step Z^T = Z^{-1} for a non-square Z makes (SMW2) not equivalent to (SMW1)
issues.why_classification: The central derivation of the method rests on this equivalence, and the guarantee changes (the method no longer optimises the advertised problem), requiring a new justification.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \min_{H} \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}\left(H^T \left( G^{-1} - \mu F F^T \right) H \right)
\mathcal{L}(H, \Lambda, \mu) = \frac{1}{2}\text{Tr}(H^T G^{-1} H) - \text{Tr}(\Lambda^T (F^T H)) - \frac{\mu}{2} \|F^T H\|_F^2

issues.failure_explanation: For a minimisation problem the augmented-Lagrangian penalty is +mu/2 ||F^T H||^2. The paper subtracts it, derives the gradient, KKT system and Lambda=0 subproblem with G^{-1} - mu FF^T, which is unbounded below and penalises nothing for large mu, and then (SMW3) uses G^{-1} + mu FF^T with no explanation. Thus SMW3 does not follow from the displayed derivation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the Lagrangian to +mu/2 ||F^T H||_F^2 and redo the gradient and subproblem; or present (SMW3) directly as a quadratic-penalty formulation with mu to infinity.
issues.overall_effect: The step from the constrained problem to (SMW3) is not derived; only the final +mu form is a sensible penalty formulation.
issues.title: Augmented Lagrangian derivation has the penalty sign reversed and then switches sign without justification
issues.why_classification: A short sign correction through the derivation yields exactly the final formula (SMW3); no other claim changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Therefore the eigenvalues of $B=\frac{1}{2}(D^{-1}W+WD^{-1})$ belong in $[-1,1]$
$G_{rw}$ has real eigenvalues and is generalized positive definite. That is $\bm{x}^T G_{rw}\bm{x} >0$

issues.failure_explanation: The bound |x^T D^{-1}W x|/x^T x <= 1 uses that eigenvalues of D^{-1}W lie in [-1,1], but D^{-1}W is non-normal, so its numerical range under the Euclidean inner product can exceed its spectral radius. For the 3-vertex path, B has eigenvalue 0.75*sqrt(2) > 1. For a star with 15 leaves, B has eigenvalues +/-16/(2*sqrt(15)) = +/-2.066, so B+2I has a negative eigenvalue and x^T G_rw x < 0 for some x. The positive-definite claim is false in general. The proof also argues '>= 0' while the statement asserts '> 0'.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the positive-definiteness claim and keep only real (positive) eigenvalues via similarity to G_sym, or restrict the statement to graphs with bounded degree heterogeneity.
issues.overall_effect: The generalized positive-definiteness of G_rw (needed, e.g., for the hypothesis of thm:added-1 and for the optimisation framework) is not established and fails for strongly degree-heterogeneous graphs. The real-eigenvalue part remains true by similarity to A_sym.
issues.title: Claim that G_rw is positive definite rests on a false numerical-range bound; counterexample exists
issues.why_classification: The false part is separable; a weakened theorem keeps the real-eigenvalue conclusion, but the framework hypotheses for rw must be handled differently.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We notice that $\mathcal{W}P$ is symmetric.

issues.failure_explanation: Right-multiplication by an invertible matrix preserves the column space, not the row space: the row space of F^T D^{-1} is D^{-1}range(F), which differs from range(F) unless range(F) is D^{-1}-invariant. The identity F^T D^{-1} (I - P_F) = 0 therefore holds only when D^{-1}F lies in range(F) (e.g. D = 2I as in Figure 1), and fails for general degrees. All subsequent simplifications of P (replacing F^T D^{-1} W F etc.) and the symmetry of W P used to get similarity to a symmetric matrix depend on it. Without the identity, U_rw = (I-N)D^{-1}W-type operator is not shown to be similar to a symmetric matrix.

failure_location.quote: multiplying by it from the right does not change the row space

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that D^{-1}F lies in range(F) (so the identity and the rest of the proof hold), or give a new argument; otherwise drop the guarantee for the RW variant.
issues.overall_effect: The real-eigenvalue guarantee for U_rw (and hence a well-defined top-k eigenproblem for the RW variant) is unproven for general graphs and groupings.
issues.title: Proof of real eigenvalues of U_rw uses a false row-space identity (F^T D^{-1} = F^T D^{-1} P_F)
issues.why_classification: A restriction of scope supported by the existing computation keeps a (weaker) theorem, but the general guarantee for the RW variant is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State Construct the fairness-adjusted matrix $U_{\text{sym}} = G_{\mathrm{sym}} - M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G_{\mathrm{sym}}$
P = F(F^T GF)^{-1}F^T G \quad \text{and} \quad U =G-GP.

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation gives U = G - GF(F^T G F)^{-1}F^T G, which needs M = GF. The algorithm instead takes M = G^{-1}F, producing G - G^{-1}F(F^T G^{-1}F)^{-1}F^T G, which is not the same matrix and is generally non-symmetric. Thm thm:added-3 (U_sym symmetric, real eigenvalues) concerns the derived U, not this one, so the eigenvector computation's guarantees do not transfer. It also requires inverting a dense G, contradicting the stated sparse cost analysis.

failure_location.quote: \State Compute the projection matrix $M = G_{\mathrm{sym}}^{-1} F$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Step 2 by M = G F (and use M (F^T M)^{-1} F^T G in Step 3), matching the derivation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated algorithm does not implement the derived operator or inherit its symmetry and real-spectrum properties.
issues.title: Fair-SMW pseudocode computes M = G^{-1}F, which gives a matrix different from (and non-symmetric unlike) the derived U
issues.why_classification: A local replacement of one line in the pseudocode aligns it with the derived formula and preserves all claims.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $G^{-1} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ is a symmetric matrix (implying $G$ is also symmetric and invertible)
given a matrix $G$ that is invertible with positive eigenvalues

issues.failure_explanation: The derivation (trace problems with orthonormal H, rewriting min of H^T M H as max of H^T M^{-1} H, top-k eigenvectors as maximisers) assumes G, hence U, symmetric positive definite. G_rw is non-symmetric, so Tr(H^T U H) sees only the symmetric part, the inverse-swap fails, and eigenvectors of U_rw need not be orthonormal or optimal. Real eigenvalues alone do not restore this. For G_aff = W + nI no spectral theorem is given; for weighted W (the stated input) it can be indefinite or singular, e.g. W = [[0,10],[10,0]] gives W+2I with eigenvalue -8.

failure_location.quote: we can construct two alternative algorithms by substituting $G_{\text{sym}}$ with either $G_{\text{rw}} = D^{-1} W + 2 I$ or $G_{\text{aff}} = W+nI$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State and verify the hypotheses (e.g. weights bounded so W+nI is positive definite) for AFF, and treat RW as a heuristic or symmetrise it, with an explicit statement of what is guaranteed.
issues.overall_effect: The optimality/validity of the RW variant, and of the AFF variant for general weighted graphs, is unsupported. These are the variants highlighted in the experiments.
issues.title: RW and AFF variants are used outside the derivation's hypotheses (symmetric positive definite G) without justification
issues.why_classification: Contained additional hypotheses/arguments or a weakened guarantee suffice, without redoing the overall framework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \leq \frac{\sum_{i,j} W_{ij}(\bm{y}_i^2 + \bm{y}_j^2)}{\sum_j \bm{y}_j^2 d_j}

issues.failure_explanation: The proof yields only the upper bound 2 (the statement's prose says 'bounded by 2'), yet the formal claim asserts equality. Equality fails for non-bipartite graphs: for the unweighted triangle K_3, L_sym has eigenvalues 0, 1.5, 1.5, so the supremum is 1.5 < 2. Equality holds only when some component is bipartite.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace '= 2' by '<= 2' (and note equality iff bipartite component).
issues.overall_effect: The theorem as stated is false; the bound lambda <= 2 that is actually used for the eigenvalue range in the proof of thm:added-2 remains valid.
issues.title: Theorem claims the normalized Rayleigh quotient has supremum exactly 2, but the proof only shows <= 2
issues.why_classification: Changing the equality to an inequality is a one-line fix that preserves everything the paper uses.
